audit.whatIsWrong: Eight places credit Lillia with a 'W bounce' and 'E move speed'. Watch Out! Eep! is a 500-range AoE that deals heavy damage in the centre — there is no bounce and no dash. Swirlseed is a rolling seed that damages, slows and reveals — it grants no move speed. The stacking move speed is on Blooming Blows' passive.
audit.why: The page tells the player Lillia dodges Tangle-Barbs with a mobility spell she does not have. What actually beats the root is stacked move speed she earns by hitting spells, which means the counterplay is throwing E before she has stacks, not waiting out a dash that never comes.
audit.corrected: whys[0], whys[2], whys[3], spikes[3].text, wants.foe[0], wants.foe[1], content.early and content.mid now name Blooming Blows' stacking speed and Swirlseed's slow.
sources: kit: Lillia Q text and flags
kit: Lillia E text, range 700, cd 12

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] calls Tangle-Barbs 'a distance-scaled root' and content.early says 'her root scales with distance'. Riot's text says the tangle grows larger, faster and roots for longer if it kills an enemy or passes through a champion — travel distance is not the trigger.
audit.why: A player who thinks distance is the variable throws E from max range at an isolated target. The actual upgrade comes from threading it through the wave or a champion, which is a different aim entirely.
audit.corrected: whys[2] and content.early now state the pass-through-a-champion growth rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Skill on rows 3, 4-5 and 2+ items and Neeko at 6, while the packet chart and the already-applied mirror read Lillia, Lillia, Skill, Neeko. whys[6] also contradicts the mirror outright, claiming Lillia reclaims the game at 2+ items.
audit.why: Levels 3-5 are Lillia's real window — she farms safe and kites on stacked speed while Neeko has no all-in. At 2+ items it inverts: Pop Blossom is AoE against a Lilting Lullaby that only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust, so grouped fights are Neeko's.
audit.corrected: win[2], win[3] to Lillia, win[4] to Skill, win[6] to Neeko as matched pairs with ratings rescaled inverse to the mirror's, and whys[6] plus content.late rewritten to agree.

edits.before: Level 1 you have nothing on Lillia — single-target Q only, and she just kites you with W bounce and stacks her passive burn, so concede it and last-hit at max Q range. The lane opens up at 3: with Q + Tangle-Barbs (E) you can finally root her, and because her root scales with distance, sniping her as she walks up to farm is your cleanest pin. Don't throw E into open space chasing her dash — she'll W-bounce away and you'll have nothing for the gank that follows.
edits.after: Level 1 you have nothing on Lillia — single-target Q only, and she kites you on Blooming Blows' stacking move speed while her passive burn ticks, so concede it and last-hit at max Q range. The lane opens up at 3: with Q + Tangle-Barbs (E) you can finally root her, and because the tangle grows after passing through a champion, threading it at her through the wave is your cleanest pin. Don't throw E into open space chasing her — she walks out on stacked speed and you have nothing for the gank that follows.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are genuinely hers: she farms safely, kites your Q with E move speed and W bounce, and her DOT ticks you down if you over-extend, so trade for waveclear and hold your E. At 6 everything flips — Pop Blossom converts a landed Tangle-Barbs into a full burst combo, and you can channel it from W invisibility or behind a clone so she can't pre-empt it with R sleep. Bait her Lullaby (R) or E first, then root, Q-bloom, and slam.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are genuinely hers: she farms safely, kites your Q on stacked Blooming Blows speed, slows you with Swirlseed, and her passive ticks you down if you over-extend, so trade for waveclear and hold your E. At 6 it evens — Pop Blossom converts a landed Tangle-Barbs into a full burst combo, and while you are disguised the wind-up is hidden outright. Her Lilting Lullaby answers it, but only on targets already carrying Dream Dust.

edits.before: Your first-item Liandry's spike owns the mid-game pick window — clustered fights are where your AoE burst and her squishy body lose to one Pop Blossom. But the longer it goes, the more she reclaims it: at 2+ items her DOT, W bounce, and R sleep let her kite a single Neeko rotation she's already weathered, and she out-roams your disguise pressure. Convert your 6-and-first-item lead into objectives and pick offs before the game turns into her kiting clinic.
edits.after: Your first-item Liandry's spike owns the mid-game pick window — clustered fights are where your AoE burst and her squishy body lose to one Pop Blossom. And the longer it goes the more that holds: at 2+ items a disguised Pop Blossom into a grouped team beats anything her single-target Lilting Lullaby sets up, since the sleep needs Dream Dust on those targets first. Convert into objectives and picks, and take fights five-versus-five rather than chasing her kite on the side.

edits.before: - Lillia Blooming Blows: matchup-defining — Her kiting speed stacks — catch her early in the chase or not at all. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W clone + disguise has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Lillia Blooming Blows: matchup-defining — 6s at rank 1, its edge deals true damage, and every spell hit stacks her move speed, so armour and MR read this trade wrong. - Lilting Lullaby is 150s and only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust.

notes: The 'W bounce' invention ran through eight fields and is worth checking on Lillia's other pages — Watch Out! Eep! is a stationary AoE, and the mobility players remember is Blooming Blows' passive move-speed stacking. The Lilting Lullaby precondition matters too: it can only drowsy targets that already have Dream Dust from her hitting them with a skill, so a Neeko who has not been touched cannot be slept out of Pop Blossom.
